title: Tanzanian Mixed Meat Stew
community: Popular at Tanzanian celebrations and large gatherings
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Mchuzi wa Nyama Mchanganyiko — Tanzanian mixed meat stew with beef, goat, and chicken cooked together in one rich spiced sauce. The celebration stew that serves everyone — every guest gets the protein of their preference in one pot.
longDesc: Mixed meat stew is the feast stew — when a large gathering requires one pot to please everyone, the mixed meat preparation ensures that goat lovers, chicken lovers, and beef lovers all find their preference in the same magnificent sauce.
steps: Brown beef and goat together first — they take longer. Remove.
Add garlic, ginger, all spices, tomatoes. Cook 10 minutes.
Return beef and goat. Add water. Simmer 40 minutes.
All meats should be falling-tender. Adjust seasoning.
chefTips: Add chicken later — it cooks faster than beef and goat.
A very large pot is essential — this is a feast preparation.
commonMistakes: Adding chicken too early — it overcooks.
cookingScience: Different meats have different collagen content and cooking times. Goat and beef (higher collagen) need 60—75 total minutes; chicken (lower collagen, smaller muscle fibres) needs only 25—30 minutes. Staggered addition ensures all are perfectly cooked simultaneously.
sustainabilityTips: Mixing proteins reduces the total quantity of any single meat required — a sustainable approach to large-scale cooking.
healthBenefits: Multiple protein sources provide complete amino acid profile.
culturalNote: Mixed meat stew is Tanzania's most generous celebration dish — the pot that ensures every guest is honoured regardless of their meat preference. It is the food of true Tanzanian hospitality.
